children: Chicago Mercantile Exchange live and feeder cattle futures ended higher on Thursday amid short covering, a stronger cash market and an increase in the volume of boxed beef being sold, traders said.
settled 1.975 cents higher at 217.825 cents per pound. CME October feeder cattle
rose 1.725 cents to 327.55 cents per pound.
"We held lows last week and we were able to build back from that," said Matthew Wiegand, broker at FuturesOne. "Shorts that came in during the late summer slide exited and it's helped boost futures."
Wholesale beef was weaker, with choice cuts of boxed beef down $2.97 at $377.80 per hundredweight (cwt) Thursday, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
Select cuts of boxed beef fell 69 cents to $351.65 per cwt.
Demand has remained resilient after the end of the summer grilling season, as retailers prepare for fall.
During an investor conference on Thursday, Tyson Foods CFO Curt Calaway said the U.S. cattle herd is rebuilding, but not as fast as it had in previous rebounds.
In pork, the most actively traded October lean hog contract (LHV26) closed 0.075 cent higher at 83.15 cents per pound, reflecting a market searching for positive news to support an upward trend.
The USDA reported wholesale pork carcass values at $91.43 per cwt, down $2.20.
